title: Chemistry — Energetics
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). Terms and clues: C5#c11 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C5#c12 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; C5.2#xt3 term and clue written for the game; C5#c10 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: C5#q01, C5#q07, C5#q02, C5#q09, C5#q05, C5#q10, C5#q06, C5#q11, C5#q12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Combustion (burning)
items.clue: The reaction of a fuel with oxygen.

items.label: Conservation of energy
items.clue: It cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.

items.label: Endothermic
items.clue: Describes a change that takes in energy from the surroundings.

items.label: Thermal decomposition
items.clue: A substance breaks down into simpler substances when it is heated.

questions.stem: Steam from a kettle condenses into water on a cold window. What happens to energy as the steam condenses?

options.text: The steam takes in energy from the window
No energy moves, as it is just water
Cold flows from the glass to the steam
The steam gives out energy to the window

questions.explanation: Yes. Condensing gives energy out: as the steam turns into water, energy is transferred from it to the colder window.

questions.stem: What happens in an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Energy is given out to the surroundings
Cold is given out to the surroundings
Energy is taken in from the surroundings
Energy is used up and then destroyed

questions.explanation: Yes. In an endothermic reaction energy is transferred from the surroundings into the reacting chemicals, so the temperature of the surroundings falls.

questions.stem: Pure water is boiling in a pan, and the hob stays on. What happens to the water's temperature while it boils?

options.text: It stays at its boiling point
It keeps rising as it is heated
It falls as heat leaves in bubbles
It falls as the energy is used up

questions.explanation: Yes. While pure water boils, its temperature stays at its boiling point (100 °C at normal air pressure). The energy from the hob turns more water into steam.

questions.stem: Which of these is an endothermic chemical reaction?

options.text: Ice melting into water in a warm drink
A candle burning once a match lights it
Hydrochloric acid neutralising an alkali
Heating calcium carbonate until it breaks down

questions.explanation: Yes. Heating calcium carbonate until it breaks down is thermal decomposition, which is endothermic: the calcium carbonate takes in energy from the flame as it breaks down into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: On a cool, cloudy day a puddle slowly dries up. No heater or sunshine warms it. What happens to energy as the water evaporates?

options.text: Energy is taken in from the surroundings
None is needed, as nothing hot is near it
It is given out as the particles escape
Cold goes into the water from the cool air

questions.explanation: Yes. Evaporation always takes in energy. With no heater or sunshine, the energy comes from the surroundings: the ground and the air.

questions.stem: A hand warmer contains iron powder. When it is opened, the iron reacts with oxygen in the air and the pack warms up. Which is correct?

options.text: Exothermic: it creates new energy from nothing
Exothermic: it transfers energy to your hands
Endothermic: it takes in energy and heats up
Endothermic: it warms the things around it

questions.explanation: Yes. The iron reacting with oxygen gives out energy, which is transferred to the pack and your hands. A reaction that warms its surroundings is exothermic.

questions.stem: Pure iron melts and freezes at 1538 °C. Liquid iron poured into a mould turns solid at this temperature. What happens to energy?

options.text: It is taken in from the mould and from the air
None, as nothing can freeze when that hot
It is used up as the liquid iron sets
It is given out to the mould and the air

questions.explanation: Yes. Liquid iron turning solid is freezing, and freezing gives out energy. The energy is transferred to the colder mould and air.

questions.stem: A gas fire needs a spark to light it. Then it keeps burning by itself and warms the room. What type of reaction is the burning, and why?

options.text: Exothermic: once lit, it gives energy to the room
Endothermic: it needs energy from a spark to start
Exothermic: it passes on the spark's energy
Endothermic: it gives out energy to the room

questions.explanation: Yes. The spark only starts the reaction. Once lit, burning gives out far more energy than the spark supplied and keeps going by itself, so it is exothermic.

questions.stem: Which of these is an exothermic chemical reaction?

options.text: Steam condensing on a cold window
Heating copper carbonate in a flame
Respiration in your muscle cells
Citric acid with bicarbonate of soda

questions.explanation: Yes. Respiration is a chemical reaction in cells that gives out energy, which keeps your body warm and lets your muscles work.
